- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. The engineering-memory MCP server is connected and responding, but it has no stored data for this repository yet — every query (`get_repo_conventions`, `find_similar_rejected_patterns`, `summarize_personal_review_history`) returns empty across a few repository-identifier variants (`TRACE`, `trace-watai/trace`).

So there isn't an engineering-memory-derived convention list I can hand you right now. That said, the repo's own `CLAUDE.md` doubles as the convention source of truth for PRs here — the concrete checklist is:

- **Linear ticket link** in the PR description
- **Tests included**, and `scripts/check_repo.sh` passing (ruff check + format + pytest + pipeline smoke)
- **Schema version bump** if you touched any versioned schema (`TaskSpec`, `TraceEvent`, etc.) — plus updated consumers/tests in the same PR
- **`fixtures/expected/` changes explained in the PR body** — silent updates get reverted
- **No scenario content in `src/`** (customer names, domain specifics belong in `fixtures/`)
- **Branch naming**: `trace-harness/<feature>` or `trace-harness/tra-<id>-<feature>`
- If your change touches the **runner ↔ environment ↔ trace seam**, tag Rupert, Samrath, and yourself as reviewers (`ToolEnvironment` protocol, side-effect classes, event payloads)
- Since you're about to touch `tests/test_regression.py`: `TaskSpec`/`FixtureScript` fixture edits need `pytest -k fixture` passing, and any new fixture needs the full task/docs/script/expected wiring per the fixture authoring checklist

If you want, I can also run `predict_review_feedback` once you have an actual diff staged — that's the pre-PR gate this repo's CLAUDE.md calls for, separate from the (currently empty) conventions lookup.
